ratio_rule_notes: Integer arithmetic only (no floats). comparison GT is strictly greater-than. If baseline_record_count is 0 the rule never triggers. threshold_percent is a whole number 0-100.

gate_rules.description: Session gate_decision. Only violations with effect_scope SESSION participate. BLOCK is sticky for the session and can never be downgraded.
algorithm: if any recorded violation has decision BLOCK and effect_scope SESSION -> BLOCK
elif any recorded violation has decision REQUIRE_APPROVAL and effect_scope SESSION -> REQUIRE_APPROVAL

session_block_lockout.description: After a session-level BLOCK: mutating tools (read_only=false in tools.json) are rejected with 403 POLICY_BLOCK (details.reason=SESSION_BLOCKED); read-only tools, /complete and /rollback remain available; /commit is always rejected.

webhook_scan.known_limitation: Obfuscated secrets (base64, split strings, other encodings) are not detected in the MVP.

redaction.description: Applied to tool arguments, webhook payloads, free-text fields (agent_name, task_description, agent_summary, reviewer, reason), policy explanations, error messages/details, manifests, metadata storage and logs. Never applied to invoice row values (mutation before/after), because commit replays them verbatim; instead update_invoice rejects secret markers in notes (422 SECRET_IN_ARGUMENT) and the seed must not contain markers.
redaction.rule: Any string value containing a secret marker is replaced entirely by string_value_replacement; any object key containing a marker is replaced by object_key_replacement.

policies.description: Deleting more than 80% of baseline database records requires explicit human approval before commit. 400 of 500 (exactly 80%) does not trigger; 401 and 420 do.
policies.rationale: Agreed MVP requirement: removing a super-majority of the dataset must be reviewed by a human. The 420/500 (84%) demo case must require approval. Strictly greater-than so that exactly 80% does not trigger.

policies.description: Updating more than 25% of baseline database records requires explicit human approval before commit. 125 of 500 (exactly 25%) does not trigger; 126 does.
policies.rationale: Retained at 25% from v1.0.0 and intentionally NOT aligned with POL-001. Thresholds are independent per-operation controls, not a severity ordering. A broad update changes many records without removing them, so it can corrupt financial data at scale while resembling routine maintenance; a lower tripwire asks for human review earlier. The value is an MVP placeholder pending business input; changing it does not affect the 80% deletion requirement.

policies.description: Any staged webhook whose url, event_type or payload contains a configured secret marker (such as sk_live_DEMO_REDACTED) is blocked immediately and never staged or dispatched.
policies.rationale: Secret exfiltration attempt: the session is considered compromised, so the session gate becomes BLOCK.

policies.description: Staging a webhook whose hostname is not exactly listed in allowed_webhook_domains is blocked immediately.
policies.rationale: Unapproved destination: treated as an exfiltration attempt, so the session gate becomes BLOCK. Exact hostname match only; no wildcard or subdomain matching.

policies.description: Any tool invocation not present in the tools.json registry receives a tool-level BLOCK (400 INVALID_TOOL) and is recorded as a violation. It does not by itself block the session.
policies.rationale: The unknown call is never executed, so nothing in the session is tainted; an agent that hallucinates a tool name must not lose the whole session. The violation stays visible to the reviewer and raises risk_summary.overall_risk_level.
